text:
sarah-support: Heads up — customer ACME just escalated a P99/latency issue on their Dedicated pool dp-88. Started ~10:28 PDT during a traffic ramp, p95 ~2s -> 3s, p99 spiked from 4s -> ~22s. Customer experience: timeouts on interactive endpoints. Ticket #CS-12487.
lee-support: logged with priority=P1 and notified CS manager. Customer says it started after their morning ramp (no config changes on their side). They reported ~30% increase in error rate (5xx) during the spike. :frowning:
jamie-eng-sre: Can you paste a quick repro / curl and the exact pool id? I'll pull metrics. Also need the last 30m of attach/boot metrics: attach_lag_ms, cold_gpu_count, provisioning_queue_length.
sarah-support: repro (from customer's environment):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"rwd-open-7b","input":"ping"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Pool: dp-88, region: us-west-2a. Customer says latency worsens when they scale from 50->200 concurrent requests.
jamie-eng-sre: grabbing metrics now. Quick snapshot (last 20m): attach_lag_p95=18s, attach_lag_p99=40s, cold_gpu_count=6, provisioning_queue_len=14. Autoscaler provision rate peaked and stalls when queue > 10. Also seeing a burst of concurrent attach attempts from dp-88 owners.
ali-runtime: I pulled runtime logs for hosts serving dp-88. Seeing repeated slow container startup / kernel image pulls. Example snippet:
```
2026-03-17T17:27:02Z host-137 kernel: gpu-init-time=42000ms image-pull=30000ms kv-cache-miss
2026-03-17T17:27:05Z runtime: model-load-start id=dp-88 inst=xx
2026-03-17T17:27:36Z runtime: model-ready id=dp-88 inst=xx warmup=31.2s
```
Also a handful of preempt events reported by the hypervisor which correlate with longer attach times.
maria-platform: FYI we rolled a change to the autoscaler yesterday evening: default attach_concurrency increased from 6 -> 20 to improve throughput. That can cause a fanout of simultaneous attach requests when a few clients ramp, leading to thundering warmups and provisioning queue saturation. We also had a transient spike on our image registry which increased image-pull times ~2x for ~12 minutes at 10:25-10:37.
ashley-engruntime: That matches the warmup times. When many attaches hit the same node, the kernel/image layer serializes pulls causing long waits for subsequent attaches — increases p99 dramatically. Reproduced locally by firing 50 concurrent attaches to a single host.
jamie-eng-sre: Immediate mitigation options (short-term):
- throttle attach_concurrency back to 6 for affected autoscaler group (rollback platform change) ✅
- add 2 warm standby GPUs to dp-88 reserved pool (pre-warmed) to absorb ramp ✅
- enable customer-specific route to hosted fallback model for critical traffic (opt-in) — needs prod approval
- temporary per-customer attach rate limiter: max 3 new attaches/sec
ali-runtime: also recommend bumping local image registry retry/backoff to reduce serializing waits (small config change, can deploy in ~30m). We'll collect the slow-start host IDs and drain them for a quick repro and restart.
maria-platform: I'll roll the attach_concurrency rollback as an emergency config change and drop the default to 6 for the next 2 hours. If that doesn't cut p99 we'll forcibly gate attaches per pool. Starting now.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-88, paging oncall (eng-sre).
jamie-eng-sre: Owners & next steps:
- jamie-eng-sre: lead investigation + metric collection, create graphs for p95/p99, attach_lag, queue_len, cold_gpu_count (ETA 15m)
- ali-runtime: collect host-level logs and list of hosts with warmup>20s, plan drain+restart where safe (ETA 20m)
- maria-platform: rollback attach_concurrency config (in progress) and monitor (ETA 10m)
- ashley-engruntime: prepare the short-term reserved-capacity bump (coordinate with capacity team) (ETA 25m)
- sarah-support/lee-support: communicate mitigations to customer and offer hosted fallback link, update ticket CS-12487 (ETA 10m)
sarah-support: Noted — messaging to customer: explaining we've identified an autoscaler concurrency change + image-registry spike causing warmup thundering; we are rolling a rollback + adding standby GPUs; will follow up in 20m. Sending now.
lee-support: Customer replied — appreciates quick action and asked if this will recur. Asked for a postmortem timeline. :thumbsup:
jamie-eng-sre: Postmortem plan: collect timeline, root cause (concurrent attaches + image registry slowdown), mitigation (rollback, rate-limiting, prewarming policy), and long-term fixes (regional registry redundancy, smarter attach backoff, cohort-based warmup). I'll draft and share in #postmortems once stabilized.
ashley-engruntime: Long-term engineering actions to propose: 1) per-pool attach token bucket; 2) proactive standby GPU warmup thresholds based on ramp prediction; 3) staggered image pulls / registry cache priming.
ali-runtime: For reproducibility, I checked with a local stress test: 200 concurrent requests -> attach queue blows > 30 and p99 > 30s. I'll add the repro steps to the incident ticket.
jamie-eng-sre: Current status: attach_concurrency rollback started (maria), image-registry latency resolved by infra (partial), added 2 warm GPUs to dp-88 (ashley, in progress). Monitoring p99 now.
sarah-support: Update for customer: "We've applied a rollback to our autoscaler config, added warm capacity, and mitigated registry delays. We're still monitoring p99 — next update in 15 minutes." Sent.
oncall-bot: Monitor alert: p99 for dp-88 dropped from 22s -> 6.4s within 7 minutes of mitigations. (alert cleared)
lee-support: Customer confirms service is responding normally for now. They asked for a post-incident call; scheduling.
jamie-eng-sre: Closing notes: immediate mitigation worked. Follow-ups: postmortem doc + action items assigned to platform/runtime/capacity. I'll update INC-2026-0317-88 and CS-12487 with RCA draft. Thanks all. :tada:
